answer: Cheap clones used to flood a courier roll by reprinting one sponsor mark. An oasis desk now lets a settled key spend only one lotus chop every 72 hours, and the newcomer must park a unique kernel disk in a public tray and check in six times, forty minutes apart, while 41 units stay locked. Peers replay the tray clock and the chop serial; the lock releases after the sixth unique stamp. If one chop or tray is reused, both deposits burn and the sponsor forfeits its next two chops, so minting a herd costs scarce time and introduction rights, not just cheap keys.
